patch.value: Daily auto-release never runs in its declared window: all 84 scheduled runs fired 2.5-4 hours after the cron time, so the release clock is undocumented drift

Measured 2026-07-27 against the live workflow history. auto-release.yml declares schedule cron "35 2 * * *" and has declared exactly that value in every commit that touched the file since 2026-06-24. The GitHub API reports 84 runs for event=schedule. Not one of them started inside the declared window. The twenty most recent scheduled starts range from 05:10:04Z to 06:29:57Z, clustering near 05:35Z, which is a systematic lag of roughly three hours rather than the few minutes of jitter the platform documents. The declared cron is therefore not a description of when the project releases; it is a value nothing has ever validated against observed behaviour. Two consequences follow. First, the same-day guard computes its date key at run time, not at scheduled time, so the boundary that enforces one automatic release per day is anchored to a drifting instant that no configuration states. Second, any operator reading the workflow file forms a false expectation of the release window, and the release-health reminder that asks whether the daily release happened has no declared instant to compare against.

The observed scheduled start time is measured against the declared cron and the divergence is reported rather than assumed to be jitter; The release window is expressed as a policy the project can assert, so a run that starts outside it is a detectable condition rather than an invisible one; The same-day release guard keys off an instant whose definition is stated in the workflow and does not silently move with platform scheduling lag; The release-health verification procedure names the window it expects, so a missing release is distinguishable from a late one
Make the automatic release clock an asserted, observable contract instead of an unvalidated cron literal
Operators and agents can tell a late release from a failed one, and the one-release-per-day guarantee rests on a stated instant

The 2026-07-27 release was not produced by the schedule at all; it was driven by two manual dispatches, and the scheduled run for the day will find the work already done and skip, which reads as success
GitHub Actions hosted runners, unbraind/pm-cli, workflow auto-release.yml, measured via the workflow runs API filtered to event=schedule

Run: gh api "repos/unbraind/pm-cli/actions/workflows/auto-release.yml/runs?event=schedule&per_page=100" --jq ".workflow_runs[].created_at" and compare every value against the cron literal in .github/workflows/auto-release.yml
Scheduled auto-release runs start within a small, stated tolerance of the declared cron window, or the divergence is surfaced
All 84 scheduled runs started 2.5 to 4 hours late; the declared 02:35Z window has never once been observed
